title: Prefix-prioritized reclamation: snapshot-consistent LRU+TTL arbitration for KV GPU caches
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: As continuous batching increases peak in-flight KV cache pressure on GPUs, simple LRU or TTL-only eviction can violate prefix isolation guarantees and introduce correctness regressions for concurrent requests. We need an eviction arbitration that prioritizes prefix affinity (hot prompts) while guaranteeing snapshot-consistent reads for in-flight requests and keeping GPU memory fragmentation low.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction algorithm implemented in runtime that composes LRU eviction with per-prefix priority and TTL arbitration
In-flight requests must observe a stable prefix view: reads cannot observe partially-evicted prefix state (atomicity invariant)
No regressions in end-to-end latency SLOs for 95th and 99th percentile beyond 10% change vs baseline under same load profile
Peak GPU memory usage reduced by at least 6% for mixed short/long-sequence workloads in internal benchmark
Automated fuzzing harness validates atomicity invariant across 100k randomized sequences without discovered violations
Design doc, RFC, and PR reviewed and approved by Runtime, Serving, and QA owners
implementation_plan: 1) Design: define 'prefix priority score' combining recency (LRU rank), TTL slack, and prefix hit-rate; document formula and invariants (week 1)
2) Atomicity guard: implement versioned tombstones + lease token for entries under eviction to prevent mid-request reclamation (week 2)
3) Batch-aware reclamation: integrate with continuous batching coordinator so eviction scheduling considers current batch window and KV pinning (week 2)
4) Compaction pass: GPU-side slab compaction tweak to reduce fragmentation after aggressive evictions (week 3)
5) Tests: unit tests for lease semantics, integration tests with multi-request scenarios, and fuzz harness for randomized eviction order (week 3)
6) Performance: run benchmark suite (chatty short-turn vs long-token streams) and iterate thresholds (week 4)
7) Rollout: staged canary in dedicated fleet with telemetry toggles; monitor prefix-miss rate, evictions/sec, and request error increases (week 5)
8) Postmortem and tuning: collect data, adjust priority formula and TTL defaults, ship runtime-1.21 changelog (week 6)
decisions: Use combined LRU+TTL priority rather than a strict TTL-first policy to avoid evicting frequently re-accessed short-prefixs
Lease-based in-flight guard chosen over synchronous blocking to avoid increasing tail latency during eviction windows
Keep priority scoring computation on CPU control plane and push only eviction decisions to GPU to minimize kernel changes
Expose two knobs: 'prefix_priority_weight' and 'lease_timeout_ms' in runtime config for ops tuning
risks: Lease tokens can prolong memory retention under adversarial traffic patterns — mitigated by bounded lease_timeout and forced compaction path
Priority computation extra CPU overhead may impact host scheduling — mitigate by sampling and approximate counters
Complex interactions with continuous batching may cause temporary throughput dips during aggressive reclamation — mitigated by rate-limited evictor and canary testing
Fuzz harness may miss extremely rare interleavings; plan extended run on staging for 48h
stakeholders: Serving platform: reviews and canary owners
Bench team: perf baselines and load generator
